author: reek
body: The builder is a mutable record and appends in place, so the whole design rests on two builders started from sb-new being two records rather than one shared one. sb-new is a definition and not storage, so every mention of it re-materialises a fresh record with its own empty parts list. That is an assumption about how a zero-argument definition evaluates, and an assumption of that kind is exactly what this test exists to refuse to take on trust: if sb-new ever yielded one shared record, every builder in the program would accumulate every other builder's text and nothing else in the tree would notice.

author: reek
body: Two builders are started independently and given different text. Each must report only its own. A shared record shows up as either builder carrying the other's characters, and the length is checked as well as the text so that a builder which merely prints correctly cannot pass.
